summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was dehydrated with tachycardia on presentation. Workup for bacterial infection, including C. diff, stool culture, and ova and parasites, was negative, and symptoms were attributed to viral gastroenteritis, likely contracted from a sick family member. IV fluids were given, and empiric Zosyn was started but discontinued due to lack of bacterial source. A brief course of cefepime was given for concern over skin secretion changes but stopped after no signs of active infection. Liver enzymes were elevated but stable, thought to be secondary to viral illness. The patient improved clinically, resumed oral intake, and was discharged home. He received the first dose of abatacept as part of a clinical trial for refractory chronic GVHD and tolerated it well. Discharge medications included oral ciprofloxacin, amoxicillin (now dosed every 12 hours), and all baseline immunosuppressive and prophylactic regimens.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
